The normal cystoscopy rules out Hunner's lesions but does not exclude Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome, which often presents with a normal bladder mucosa. To further characterize the pain syndrome, is the discomfort localized to the suprapubic region or the vulva, and do you experience pelvic floor muscle tenderness on exam?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pelvic floor exam confirms significant muscle tenderness, which explains your chronic bladder discomfort and urinary frequency as a secondary effect of pelvic floor dysfunction. Since we have ruled out infection, diabetes insipidus, and interstitial cystitis, the clinical picture strongly supports a diagnosis of pelvic floor myalgia.
